title: Catena template source
description: One hand-edited template definition: the fields of the generated templates.json (Portainer App Templates format) a human owns, plus the x-catena extension block carrying everything that format has no slot for (SSO wiring, bench membership, sizing, bilingual prose). The backup, update and restore declarations live in the compose (block.schema.json). sources/<id>.json is canonical; templates.json, catalog.json, blueprints/ and index.html are generated from it and from the compose block. An entry the registry importer wrote carries x-catena.status "imported": it publishes with stubs where a curated entry has hand-written parts, and the published catalog marks it untested.

id.description: Stable slug. MUST equal the filename stem. Used as the blueprint directory, the prefix of the app's tags and the id every consumer joins on.

type.description: Template type in the generated templates.json (Portainer App Templates format): 2, a swarm stack. Every Catena template is a swarm stack: the client host already runs a single-node swarm carrying the catena services, so a compose stack would be a second runtime beside it with none of the placement or restart policy the rest of the box is held to.

name.description: The app's stack name, equal to x-catena.app_name.

categories.description: Filter categories of the catalog. Descriptive app categories, never internal enums.

status.description: Marks an entry build/import_registry.py wrote from a third-party registry and no person has finished. Its bench pack and peak_ram_mb may be null stubs and its prose is the importer's placeholder; the published catalog flags it as untested. A curated entry carries no status.

origin.description: Where an imported entry's compose file comes from, published with the entry: the registry, the entry's title there, the repository or registry the file is copied from, that source's licence and its copyright notice. It stays once a person finishes the entry.

licence.description: SPDX identifier of the source's licence as its forge names it, NOASSERTION when it names none. A record, not a condition.

attribution.description: The copyright lines of the source's licence file, or the file's or the repository's address when there are none.

commit.description: The commit of the source the entry was read at.

path.description: The entry's path in the source at that commit.

project.description: The upstream project's repository, whose licence is the app's and was checked.

aliases.description: Entries of other registries (or the same one) that are this same app: recorded, not imported.

pending.description: What a person still settles before an imported entry is curated: the findings the app checker and the catalog lint leave on its compose file, and the choices the importer cannot make. Only an imported entry carries it.

requires_catena.description: The oldest Catena release the entry deploys and updates correctly on, for an entry that needs a newer one than some servers run. Its Portainer description and its README name it.

logo.description: Where blueprints/<id>/logo.png comes from. Present exactly when the logo is placed.

source.description: The address the picture was taken from, pinned to a commit where it is a repository.

notice.description: The line the logo owner's terms ask for, printed in the README as written.

domain.description: The web address the application is served at. Absent for an application that has none, which other applications reach inside the server; its block then names version_from.

pack.description: null only on an imported entry: it is in no bench pack.

peak_ram_mb.description: Required. The bench scheduler multiplies it by 1.15 to gate slot acquisition. null only on an imported entry, which is not measured yet.

env_required_when.description: Gates an env key on a SIBLING key being non-empty: {"RELAY_PASSWORD": "RELAY_HOST"} reads "the relay password is required only when a relay host is configured". Without it every optional credential is mandatory and the host's marketplace drops the whole template over a value nothing would read. The gate must name a key this template also defines.
